Frequently asked questions
01
What is a credit?
A credit is the unit we use to measure usage in Augment Code. For example:
A small task that uses 10 tool calls would cost around 300 credits
A complex task that requires 60 tool calls would cost around 4,300 credits
Learn more about credit-based pricing →
02
Are credits pooled?
Yes. Credits are pooled at the team level. Here is an example for a team of 20 developers on Standard Plan:
Total monthly credits: 20 users × 130,000 credits = 2,600,000 credits
Typical usage pattern:
3 power users: 330,000 credits each = 990,000 credits
10 regular users: 78,000 credits each = 780,000 credits
7 occasional users: 35,000 credits each = 245,000 credits
Total used: 2,015,000 credits (585,000 remaining)
03
Do you train on my data on a paid plan?
No. All paid plans exclude any AI training on your data as part of our Commercial Terms of Service.
04
How are you handling Security & Compliance?
We take security & compliance seriously. In addition to our rigorous encryption and access controls, we undergo annual SOC 2 audits. Visit our Security page to learn more, or head to our Trust Center to request additional details and reports.
05
What SLA and support do I get on each plan?
All paid subscriptions are covered by the same core uptime and response targets described in our SLA and Support Policy. Support channels differ by plan:
Indie & Standard: Community-based support, plus the ability to file tickets via our support portal at support.augmentcode.com. Tickets submitted through the portal are handled under our SLA.
Max: Everything in Standard, with email-based support in addition to community channels, handled under the same SLA when you file tickets through our support portal.
Enterprise: Full SLA coverage with dedicated support on top of our standard commitments.
Free & trial use: Community support only; our SLA does not apply to trials or beta usage.
Read the full SLA and Support Policy →
06
When do my credits expire?
Credits top-ups that are not part of your paid plan are valid 12 months after the date of purchase.
07
What is the difference between Code Review and Code Review Enterprise?
Code Review is available on all plans and provides AI-powered code review for GitHub pull requests. Enterprise Code Review includes additional capabilities:
Advanced Analytics: Dashboard showing reviews performed and comments addressed
User Allowlists: Control which users receive PR reviews
MCP Configuration: Connect to ticketing systems (Jira, Linear), docs (Notion), and other tools for richer context
Multi-org Support: Install on multiple GitHub organizations
Unlimited Seats & Repos: No limits on team size or connected repositories
Learn more in the docs.
